text:
Alex: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection roll earlier today p99 latency for long streaming requests spiked on prod. Not catastrophic but consistent: p50 ~34ms, p95 ~310ms, p99 ~890ms across the cluster.
Priya: ugh. saw some alerts. any idea if this is kernel mismatch or batching change?
Alex: preliminary profiling shows a working-set increase during KV cache lookup paths after the new kernel heuristics picked a fwd-kv path that touches a larger slice. Flamegraph link: https://internal/flame/180124 (internal)
Marta: that sounds like memory thrash + more GC pauses on some hosts. Which instances are affected?
Alex: mostly on the r-infer-gpu-3 pool (high mem pressure). Also queue depth for microbatches rose which exacerbates tail.
Dan: can we short-circuit long requests or prioritize short ones? We've done that before.
Priya: Suggestion: implement a dynamic safety quota that reduces max_tokens per request when local queue_depth > threshold. Quick sketch:
```
dynamic_max_tokens:
  enabled: true
  base_max: 1024
  queue_depth_threshold: 12
  reduction_factor: 0.5
  min_max: 64
```
Lina: I like that — it keeps fast customers fast and prevents a few heavy tails from trashing caches.
Marta: Also consider lowering microbatch size for routes that use KV heavily. e.g., microbatch_size 8 for stream-heavy routes vs 32 default.
Alex: Agreed. Also propose a per-route override where we set absolute max_tokens for free-tier vs enterprise: free-tier max_tokens=256, standard=512, enterprise=2048.
Dan: Could do both: dynamic safety quota + per-route cap. That should reduce p99 while preserving throughput.
InfraBot: Deploy pipeline started: canary to r-infer-gpu-3 with dynamic_max_tokens=true (PR #4839). Status: queued.
Priya: We need telemetry: new metrics for "tokens_capped_by_safety_quota" and "avg_max_tokens_applied". Add tag by route and customer_tier.
Alex: I'll add the metrics in the rollout PR and a Grafana panel for p95/p99 by route with an overlay of queue_depth.
Marta: One more observation from the profiler: KV cache miss rate spiked ~2.2x after the kernel change. Might be related to different memory residency causing more evictions.
Lina: If eviction rate high we should try sticky-cache affinity: prefer serving requests on nodes with warm caches for that model/route.
Dan: For immediate protection we should enforce a hard timeout as a last resort: request_timeout_ms = min(user_timeout_ms, 120000) and also apply early truncation for decode-heavy streams.
Priya: Early truncation policy proposal: after N tokens produced and elapsed_time > T, reduce allowed_future_tokens by factor F. We can tune N,T,F via canary.
Alex: Plan of action:
- Short-term (canary): enable dynamic_max_tokens + per-route caps on r-infer-gpu-3 (PR #4839)
- Telemetry: add tokens_capped_by_safety_quota metric + queue_depth overlay
- Medium: microbatch downgrade for KV-heavy routes + sticky-cache affinity experiment
- Long: revisit kernel-selection heuristics to avoid selecting the larger-kv-slice path for these models
Marta: timeline?
Alex: Can do canary today, monitor 6 hours, then widen if p99 drops ~2x. I'll own rollout.
Priya: SGTM. I'll help with metrics and dashboard.
Dan: I'll add a small interceptor to apply early truncation in the runtime so we don't need full config churn.
Lina: I'll pair with Dan on the interceptor; we should ensure the logic logs whether truncation happened and why (queue_depth or timeout).
Alex: Thanks all — let's watch the canary and regroup in ~6h. If we still see tail issues we'll consider temporary global max_tokens caps.
Marta: :thumbsup:
InfraBot: Canary deployed to r-infer-gpu-3. Health checks passing. Telemetry pipeline: pending metric registration.
Priya: Posting the PRs: https://internal/pulls/4839 and https://internal/pulls/4842. Will update dashboards when metrics land.
Alex: Closing loop later. For notes: add an entry in the runbook about "safety quota" so oncall can enable quickly if tails recur.
